message.content:
Civil law is a broad legal system that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be grouped into several key areas:

| Component | What it Covers | Typical Examples |
|-----------|----------------|------------------|
| **Contracts** | Rules governing agreements, obligations, and remedies when parties fail to perform. | Sale contracts, lease agreements, service contracts. |
| **Torts (Delicts)** | Liability for wrongful acts or omissions that cause harm or loss. | Negligence, defamation, product liability. |
| **Property Law** | Rights, duties, and transfer of ownership over real and personal property. | Real estate transactions, easements, mortgages. |
| **Family Law** | Regulations concerning marriage, divorce, child custody, and support. | Divorce proceedings, alimony, child custody arrangements. |
| **Inheritance & Succession** | Rules on wills, estates, and distribution of assets after death. | Probate, intestate succession, testamentary trusts. |
| **Corporate & Commercial Law** | Governance of business entities, corporate governance, and commercial transactions. | Company formation, shareholder rights, mergers & acquisitions. |
| **Consumer Protection** | Safeguards for buyers against unfair practices. | Warranty claims, deceptive advertising. |
| **Intellectual Property** | Protection of creations of the mind. | Patents, trademarks, copyrights. |
| **Administrative Law** | Oversight of government actions affecting private rights. | Licensing, permits, regulatory compliance. |
| **Procedural Law** | Rules governing how civil cases are brought and adjudicated. | Pleadings, discovery, trial procedures. |

These components interact to form a comprehensive framework that resolves disputes, protects rights, and facilitates orderly conduct in society.
